memory.title: How do workers share what they learn?
memory.body: Every project has a memory. When a worker spawns, ClaudeNest compiles the relevant context and injects it into the session. When a worker completes a task, its summary is ingested back — embedded with a local Ollama model into pgvector. The next worker starts where the last one left off.

memory.note: Embeddings are computed on your server via Ollama. Nothing is sent to a third-party embedding API.

planning.title: From a one-paragraph brief to a calibrated sprint
planning.body: Open a planning session, describe what you want to ship, and ClaudeNest drafts epics, tasks and a sprint — sized against your project's actual velocity, not a guess. Then it launches the build itself: a pool of sandboxed Claude workers claims each task, codes it and completes it autonomously, recycling to a fresh context between tasks. Finish the sprint and it opens a pull request for the work.
planning.bullet: And when things go sideways — a task bounced twice, two workers fighting over a lock — the incident coordinator spawns a Claude session to resolve it. Capped at one per hour, so it can't spiral.

what_is.title: What is ClaudeNest, exactly?
what_is.body: ClaudeNest is a self-hosted orchestration platform for Claude Code. It runs multiple Claude Code workers in parallel on the same repository and coordinates them through three mechanisms: atomic task claiming over an MCP server (20 tools), file locks enforced at edit time by Claude Code hooks, and a shared project memory backed by PostgreSQL pgvector. The server spawns interactive worker sessions, injects compiled project context at startup, and ingests each worker's completion summary back into memory — so later sessions inherit what earlier ones learned. A real-time board (epics, sprints, burndown) tracks every task over WebSockets, and iOS/Android apps (beta) expose the same terminals remotely. ClaudeNest is free to run on your own server under the PolyForm Noncommercial license; paid plans lift concurrency caps. It requires PostgreSQL with pgvector, Redis, and a Node.js agent on each machine.

0.question: Is ClaudeNest really free?
0.answer: Yes. Self-hosting is free under the PolyForm Noncommercial license, with the full feature set and a cap of 3 concurrent workers. Pro ($29/mo) raises the cap to 20 workers and unlimited projects. The caps are enforced by the server (you'll get a 403, not a nag screen).

1.question: Will my Claude subscription or API credits work?
1.answer: Yes — that's the model. Workers are real Claude Code sessions running with your own credentials: an API key or your Claude Max OAuth session. Credentials are stored encrypted (AES-256) and isolated per session, so two workers never share an auth context.

2.question: Where does my code go?
2.answer: Nowhere. ClaudeNest is self-hosted: the server runs on your infrastructure and the agent on your dev machines. Code, terminal output and embeddings stay on hardware you control. claudenest.io serves this website and the install script — nothing else.

3.question: What happens when two workers touch the same file?
3.answer: The first worker takes a lock. The second worker's edit is denied at edit time by a Claude Code hook, with the owner's name in the message, and it moves on to other work. Locks expire automatically and can be force-released. One honest caveat: if the agent can't reach the server, hooks fail open rather than freezing your session.

4.question: What do I need to run it?
4.answer: A Linux server with PHP/Laravel, PostgreSQL with the pgvector extension, and Redis. Each dev machine runs a small Node.js agent. Ollama (for local embeddings) is optional but recommended for the shared memory features.

5.question: How is this different from Claude-Flow and swarm tools?
5.answer: Different goal. Swarm tools fan out many short-lived agents from your terminal. ClaudeNest is a server: long-lived interactive sessions you can attach to from web or mobile, a persistent project memory, edit-time lock enforcement, and a real-time board. See the comparison table above.

6.question: Can I watch what a worker is doing?
6.answer: Yes. Every worker is an attachable terminal — open it in the dashboard or the mobile app, see the live output, and type into it if you need to take over.

7.question: Can I contribute?
7.answer: The source is public on GitHub — issues and PRs welcome. The license is PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0: free for personal and internal use; commercial licensing, talk to us.

docChangelog.v170Desc: Decomposing a PRD now structures the work into sprints and generates the project context, the global context stays alive as tasks complete, and the workspace lets you track the git worktree, pull requests and merge directly.
docChangelog.v170Change1: Decomposition: one sprint per wave (the first one active) and the project context (summary, architecture, conventions) generated automatically when missing.
docChangelog.v170Change2: Living global context: every completed task feeds a rolling recent-changes log and the current focus, re-injected into each recycled worker's prompt (no more frozen snapshot).
docChangelog.v170Change3: Git tracking in the workspace: branch, ahead/behind, changed files, pull-request list and direct merge (squash / merge / rebase).
docChangelog.v170Change4: Sprint finalization (pull-request creation) runs inside the bubblewrap sandbox, just like the workers.
docChangelog.v170Change5: UX: the rail's activity area is enlarged for better real-time tracking.
docChangelog.v160Desc: Workers now build your backlog end-to-end on their own — claiming, coding, completing, and recycling — each one confined to a lightweight sandbox. The planner launches the build itself, and a sprint ships as a pull request.
docChangelog.v160Change1: Autonomous workers: the server-driven pool claims, builds and completes pending tasks with zero supervision (bypassPermissions, self-sustaining loop).
docChangelog.v160Change2: Sandboxed workers: every worker runs inside a lightweight bubblewrap sandbox (no Docker) — read-all but writes confined to its own project. The agent installs it automatically.
docChangelog.v160Change3: Fresh context per task: a worker is recycled into a clean session after each completed task, so context never bloats across the backlog.
docChangelog.v160Change4: Planning agent launches execution: from the planning chat, execution_start spawns the worker pool to build the plan it just drafted.
docChangelog.v160Change5: Sprint auto-PR: completing a sprint opens a pull request for its work automatically (branch + commit + push + gh pr create) and surfaces the URL.
docChangelog.v160Change6: Resilient loop: heartbeat-independent dispatch, rate-limit cool-down with unlimited retry, in-progress task resume, and infinite agent reconnection — workers never stay stuck.
docChangelog.v160Change7: Self-healing sessions: a worker whose status update was lost is promoted back to running on its next heartbeat instead of showing as disconnected.

docDocsCookiepolicy.lead: How ClaudeNest uses cookies and local storage to ensure the security and operation of the platform.
docDocsCookiepolicy.companyAddress: SAS with capital of €10,000 — RCS Paris
docDocsCookiepolicy.s2Para1: A cookie is a small text file placed on your device (computer, tablet, smartphone) when you visit a website. It allows the site to recognize your browser and store certain information about your session.
docDocsCookiepolicy.s2Para2: In addition to cookies, browsers offer other storage technologies, such as {localStorage}, which allows web applications to store data locally in your browser, without it being automatically sent to the server with every request.
docDocsCookiepolicy.s3Intro: ClaudeNest uses only {strictlyNecessary} cookies for the platform to operate. No advertising or analytics cookies are used.
docDocsCookiepolicy.xsrfPurpose: Protection against cross-site request forgery (CSRF) attacks. Ensures that requests come from a legitimate session.
docDocsCookiepolicy.sessionPurpose: Maintains your authenticated session and stores temporary server-side state.
docDocsCookiepolicy.cookieSecurityBody: All cookies are issued with the {secure} (HTTPS only), {httpOnly} (no JavaScript access) and {sameSite} (CSRF protection) attributes.
docDocsCookiepolicy.s4Intro: ClaudeNest uses your browser's local storage (localStorage) to store certain information needed for the application to operate and to enhance your experience:
docDocsCookiepolicy.authTokenPurpose: Authentication token used to keep you signed in and authorize your API calls.
docDocsCookiepolicy.themePurpose: Stores your display preference (dark, light or system mode).
docDocsCookiepolicy.localePurpose: Stores your preferred interface language (French or English).
docDocsCookiepolicy.s4Outro: This data is stored exclusively in your browser and is never transmitted to third parties. You can delete it at any time from your browser settings.
docDocsCookiepolicy.s5Intro: In keeping with our privacy-respecting approach, ClaudeNest uses {none} of the following technologies:
docDocsCookiepolicy.absentAnalyticsBody: No Google Analytics, Matomo or any other audience tracking tool.
docDocsCookiepolicy.absentAdsBody: No advertising cookies or behavioral targeting.
docDocsCookiepolicy.absentCrossSiteBody: No third-party cookies or cross-site tracking.
docDocsCookiepolicy.absentSocialBody: No social media plugins that collect your data.
docDocsCookiepolicy.s6Intro: Under the GDPR and the ePrivacy directive, the legal basis for our use of cookies and local storage is as follows:
docDocsCookiepolicy.s6Item1: {strong} for strictly necessary cookies (session, CSRF, authentication), which are exempt from prior consent.
docDocsCookiepolicy.s6Item2: {strong} for functional storage (theme, language), where the data never leaves your browser.
docDocsCookiepolicy.noBannerBody: Because ClaudeNest uses only strictly necessary cookies and no analytics or advertising cookies, no consent banner is required under the CNIL's recommendations.
docDocsCookiepolicy.s7Intro: You can manage and delete cookies and local storage at any time. Note that deleting strictly necessary cookies will affect how the platform works.
docDocsCookiepolicy.s71Intro: Each browser offers its own settings to manage cookies. Refer to the official guides:
docDocsCookiepolicy.s72Body: To clear local storage, open your browser's developer tools (F12), go to the "Application" or "Storage" tab, then delete the entries associated with claudenest.io. You can also clear your browsing data, which removes both cookies and local storage.
docDocsCookiepolicy.warningBody: Deleting strictly necessary cookies or the authentication token will sign you out and require you to reconnect. Some features may become unavailable.
docDocsCookiepolicy.s8Intro: ClaudeNest can be self-hosted on your own infrastructure. In this case:
docDocsCookiepolicy.s8Item1: The cookies and local storage are created and managed entirely on your own server.
docDocsCookiepolicy.s8Item2: No data is sent to QR Communication or any third party.
docDocsCookiepolicy.s8Item3: You become the data controller for the cookies placed by your instance.
docDocsCookiepolicy.s8Item4: You are responsible for complying with applicable cookie regulations.
docDocsCookiepolicy.s9Intro: This cookie policy may be updated to reflect changes to the platform or the regulatory framework. In the event of a significant change:
docDocsCookiepolicy.s9Item1: The effective date at the top of this page will be updated.
docDocsCookiepolicy.s9Item2: You will be informed via the platform or by email where appropriate.
docDocsCookiepolicy.s9Item3: We encourage you to review this page regularly to stay informed of our practices.
docDocsCookiepolicy.s10Intro: For any question regarding the use of cookies on ClaudeNest, you can contact us:
docDocsCookiepolicy.footerText: This cookie policy complies with the CNIL's recommendations and the requirements of the ePrivacy directive 2002/58/EC.
docDocsCookiepolicy.footerMeta: QR Communication — Cookie policy — Effective date: April 12, 2026

docDocsPrivacypolicy.title: Privacy Policy
docDocsPrivacypolicy.leadPara: This Privacy Policy describes how QR Communication collects, uses, stores and protects your personal data when you use the ClaudeNest platform, in compliance with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR - EU Regulation 2016/679) and the French Data Protection Act of 6 January 1978 as amended.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s1Intro: The controller of the personal data collected via the ClaudeNest platform is:
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s1OpenSourcePara: ClaudeNest is also open source software designed for self-hosting. When you use an instance operated by a third party, that third party is the data controller. Please refer to its own privacy policy.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s1SelfHostedPara: For self-hosted instances, the data controller is the entity operating the server. This policy serves as a reference and template that operators must adapt to their own legal obligations.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s1DpoPara: QR Communication has appointed Mr Rony Licha as Data Protection Officer. This appointment was declared to the CNIL on 23 October 2025 and took effect on 24 October 2025.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s2Intro: ClaudeNest collects and processes the following categories of personal data, each for a specific and documented purpose.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s21NamePurpose: Display name in the interface and collaborative features
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s21PasswordPurpose: Secure authentication (bcrypt hashed, never stored in plaintext)
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s21AvatarPurpose: Profile display (sourced from OAuth providers where applicable)
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s21OauthRetention: Until account deletion or OAuth unlinking
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s22ClaudePathPurpose: Location of the Claude Code binary on the machine
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s22TokenHashPurpose: Machine authentication (hashed, never stored in plaintext)
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s22TokenHashRetention: Until machine deletion or token regeneration
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s23TerminalPurpose: Real-time display and session logs for review
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s23CommandsPurpose: Input relay between the client and the agent
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s2WarningTitle: Terminal output may contain sensitive data
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s2WarningPara: Terminal sessions may inadvertently capture sensitive information such as API keys, credentials or personal data present in your source code. ClaudeNest does not filter or mask session output. Operators must put in place appropriate data handling policies and inform their users accordingly.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s24ContentPurpose: Shared project context for multi-agent collaboration
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s24EmbeddingPurpose: Semantic similarity search via pgvector (cosine distance)
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s24EmbeddingsPara3: No data is sent to external AI services for embedding generation.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s25TotalTokensPurpose: Tracking token consumption per session and per project
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s25ContextTokensPurpose: Context window usage per Claude instance
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s26Para: ClaudeNest records an activity log for each shared project, including the instance identifier, the event type and event details (stored as JSONB). These logs are used for audit trails, debugging and collaboration visibility.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s27CredentialsPurpose: Launching your Claude Code sessions on your own machines
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s27CredentialsRetention: Until deleted by the user or account deletion
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s27PushTokenPurpose: Sending push notifications to your mobile devices
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s27PushTokenRetention: Until the device is logged out or the account is deleted
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s27Para: Your Claude credentials (Anthropic API keys, OAuth tokens) are stored encrypted (AES-256) on the server. They are used exclusively to launch your Claude Code sessions on your own machines and are never shared with third parties.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s3Intro: QR Communication processes personal data on the following legal bases, defined in Article 6(1) of the General Data Protection Regulation:
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s3ContractualPara: The processing of account data, machine data and session data is necessary for the performance of the contract between you and QR Communication (provision of the ClaudeNest platform).
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s3LegitimatePara: The processing of usage data, activity logs and performance metrics is based on our legitimate interest in maintaining and improving the platform.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s3LegitimateItem1: Token and cost tracking for transparency
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s3LegitimateItem2: Activity logs for security and audit purposes
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s3ConsentPara: Where applicable, certain processing activities require your explicit consent:
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s3ConsentItem1: OAuth linking with third-party providers (Google, GitHub)
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s3ConsentItem2: Encrypted storage of your Claude credentials (API keys / OAuth tokens) provided at your initiative
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s3LegalObligationPara: Certain data may be retained to comply with legal obligations:
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s3LegalObligationItem1: Compliance with legal data retention requirements
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s3LegalObligationItem2: Response to judicial proceedings or government requests
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s4Intro: Your personal data is used exclusively for the following purposes:
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s4Use1Para: Verifying your identity, managing sessions and enforcing authorization policies.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s4Use2Para: Connecting to your registered machines, managing PTY sessions and relaying terminal input/output.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s4Use3Para: Coordinating tasks, managing file locks and sharing context between Claude instances.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s4Use4Para: Local embedding generation and semantic search to provide relevant context to Claude instances.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s4Use5Para: Tracking token consumption and estimating costs for transparency and budget management.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s4Use6Para: Analysis of aggregated and anonymized usage data to improve features and performance.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s4NotUsedPara2: use your personal data for advertising, profiling, automated decision-making, or any purpose unrelated to the core features of the platform.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s5Intro: We retain personal data only for as long as necessary for the purposes described in this policy. The following retention periods apply:
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s5RowAccountTrigger: The user requests deletion or the account is terminated
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s5RowMachineTrigger: The user removes the machine from the platform
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s5RowSessionTrigger: Deleted by the user or account deletion
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s5RowEmbeddingsTrigger: Cascade deletion with the context chunk
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s5OutroPre: Instance operators can configure retention periods via the configuration file
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s6Intro: ClaudeNest is designed with a strong emphasis on data locality. By design, the platform minimizes external data transfers.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s61OllamaPara3: are performed entirely on-premise via Ollama.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s61OllamaEmphasis: No data is transmitted to external AI services.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s61PostgresPara: All persistent data, including vector embeddings, is stored in your local or self-managed PostgreSQL instance. No cloud database services are required.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s61RedisPara: Used for caching, session management, queue processing, and WebSocket state. All data remains in-memory on your local or self-managed Redis instance.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s61ReverbPara: Real-time communication is handled by Laravel Reverb, a self-hosted WebSocket server. No third-party WebSocket services (e.g., Pusher, Ably) are used.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s62GooglePara: If configured, Google OAuth is used for authentication. Google receives the standard OAuth flow data (authorization code, redirect URI). Only the user's email, name, and avatar URL are retrieved.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s62GithubPara: If configured, GitHub OAuth is used for authentication. GitHub receives the standard OAuth flow data. Only the user's email, name, and avatar URL are retrieved.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s62AnthropicPara: If you register your own Anthropic API key (or OAuth token), your prompts and session content are transmitted to Anthropic from your machine when Claude Code runs. This processing takes place under your control and is governed by Anthropic's terms and privacy policy. ClaudeNest stores these credentials encrypted (AES-256) and only uses them to launch your sessions on your machines.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s63Para1: ClaudeNest does not sell, rent, transfer or trade
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s63Para2: personal data to any third party, for any purpose whatsoever. We do not engage in data brokerage.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s64ScalewayPara: The official claudenest.io instance is hosted by Scaleway SAS, 8 rue de la Ville l'Évêque, 75008 Paris, France. Data is hosted in France (European Union). Scaleway acts as a processor within the meaning of Article 28 of the GDPR, under a data processing agreement.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s7Intro: Under the General Data Protection Regulation and the French Data Protection Act, you have the following rights regarding your personal data. These rights may be exercised by contacting the Data Protection Officer (DPO).
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s7AccessPara: You have the right to obtain confirmation that your personal data is being processed, and to receive a copy of that data in a structured and commonly used format.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s7AccessHow: Request a data export from your account settings or contact the DPO.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s7RectificationPara: You have the right to request the correction of inaccurate personal data and to have incomplete data completed.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s7RectificationHow: Update your profile in account settings, or contact the DPO for data you cannot edit directly.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s7ErasureTitle: Right to erasure (right to be forgotten)
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s7ErasurePara: You have the right to request the deletion of your personal data when it is no longer necessary for the purposes for which it was collected, or when you withdraw your consent.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s7ErasureHow: Delete your account via settings (cascade deletion of all associated data), or contact the DPO.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s7RestrictionPara: You have the right to request the restriction of the processing of your data in certain circumstances, for example when you contest the accuracy of the data.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s7RestrictionHow: Contact the DPO with your specific restriction request.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s7PortabilityPara: You have the right to receive your personal data in a structured, commonly used and machine-readable format (JSON), and to transmit it to another controller.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s7PortabilityHow: Use the data export feature in your account settings, which provides a JSON archive of all your data.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s7ObjectionPara: You have the right to object to the processing of your personal data based on legitimate interest, including profiling. You may also object at any time to processing for direct marketing purposes.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s7ObjectionHow: Contact the DPO. Processing will cease unless compelling legitimate grounds override your interests.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s7PostMortemPara: In accordance with Article 85 of the French Data Protection Act, you also have the right to set directives regarding the retention, erasure and disclosure of your personal data after your death.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s7ComplaintPre: If you believe that your data protection rights have been violated, you have the right to lodge a complaint with the competent supervisory authority. In France, this is the
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s7ComplaintPost: (Commission Nationale de l'Informatique et des Libertes), 3 place de Fontenoy, TSA 80715, 75334 Paris Cedex 07.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s7ResponsePre: We will respond to all legitimate requests within
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s7ResponsePost: In complex cases, this period may be extended by an additional 60 days, with prior notification.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s8IntroPre: ClaudeNest uses a minimal number of cookies and employs no third-party tracking technology. For more details, see our
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s8NotUsedItem1: Google Analytics or any other third-party analytics service
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s8Outro: Since all cookies used are strictly necessary for the operation of the platform, no cookie consent banner is required in accordance with the GDPR and the CNIL recommendations.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s9Intro: ClaudeNest implements comprehensive technical and organizational measures to protect your personal data against any unauthorized access, alteration, disclosure or destruction.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s9TransportItem1: TLS 1.3 enforced for all HTTP and WebSocket connections in production
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s9TransportItem2: HTTPS-only configuration recommended for all deployments
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s9TransportItem3: WebSocket encryption via WSS (WebSocket Secure) protocol
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s9AuthItem1: Bcrypt hashing for all passwords (never stored in plaintext)
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s9AuthItem2: SHA-256 hashing for machine tokens and API tokens
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s9AuthItem3Pre: OS Keychain storage for agent tokens via
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s9AuthItem4: Laravel Sanctum token-based authentication with scoped abilities
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s9AppItem1: CSRF protection on all web routes
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s9AppItem2: Rate limiting on all API endpoints
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s9AppItem3: Input validation via Laravel Form Requests
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s9AppItem4: Parameterized queries via Eloquent ORM (SQL injection prevention)
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s9AppItem6: No sensitive data in logs policy enforced across all components
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s9InfraItem1: Self-hosted architecture keeping data on your own infrastructure
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s9InfraItem2: Database encryption at rest (recommended for production)
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s9InfraItem3: Redis AUTH for cache and queue authentication
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s9InfraItem4: Network isolation recommended for database and cache services
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s9InfraItem5: Regular security updates via dependency management
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s9AgentItem2: No credential exposure in logs or terminal output
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s9AgentItem3: Structured logging via Pino with sensitive data filtering
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s10Para1: The official ClaudeNest instance operated by QR Communication is hosted in France with Scaleway SAS. In this configuration, no international data transfer is carried out by the publisher as part of standard operation.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s10Para2: For self-hosted instances, if the instance is hosted in one jurisdiction and accessed from another, the operator should consider the following safeguards:
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s10Item1Text: No additional safeguards required under the GDPR.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s10Item2Text: Transfers to countries subject to an adequacy decision by the European Commission are permitted without additional safeguards.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s10Item3Text: Appropriate safeguards must be put in place, such as Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) or Binding Corporate Rules (BCRs).
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s10Para3: When OAuth providers are used (Google, GitHub), authentication data may be processed in the United States. Google and GitHub have both committed to complying with the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s11Para1: ClaudeNest is a professional software development tool and is not intended for individuals under the age of 16 (or the minimum age applicable in your jurisdiction).
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s11Para2: We do not knowingly collect personal data from minors. If you learn that a minor has provided personal data to a ClaudeNest instance, please contact the DPO immediately. The data will be deleted without delay.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s12Intro: We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time to reflect changes in our practices, technology, legal requirements or other factors. In the event of a material change:
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s12Item1: The update date at the top of this page will be revised.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s12Item2: A notification will be displayed in the ClaudeNest dashboard for 30 days.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s12Item3: Registered users will be notified by email (if email notifications are enabled).
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s12Item4: For changes affecting the legal basis of processing or introducing new categories of data, we will seek renewed consent where the GDPR requires it.
docDocsPrivacypolicy.s12Outro: We encourage you to review this Privacy Policy regularly. Your continued use of ClaudeNest after changes are published constitutes acceptance of the updated policy.

docDocsConceptsArchitecture.title: Architecture Overview
docDocsConceptsArchitecture.lead: ClaudeNest v1.2 follows a distributed architecture with three main packages: a Laravel 13 server acting as the central hub, lightweight Node.js 24 agents running on developer machines, and native Expo 55 / React Native mobile apps for on-the-go access.
docDocsConceptsArchitecture.systemDesignPara1: The platform is organized around a client-server model where multiple client types (web dashboard, mobile apps, agents) communicate with a central Laravel server. The server manages authentication, session orchestration, context storage, and real-time event distribution.
docDocsConceptsArchitecture.monorepoTipBody: All three packages live in a single monorepo under {packages}. The server package includes both the Laravel backend and the Vue.js frontend SPA.
docDocsConceptsArchitecture.serverPara1: The server is a {laravel} application that serves as the central orchestration hub. It exposes a REST API for CRUD operations, hosts the Vue.js SPA dashboard, and runs a WebSocket relay via Laravel Reverb for real-time communication.

docDocsConceptsArchitecture.serverResp4: Multi-agent coordination (tasks, file locks, shared context)
docDocsConceptsArchitecture.serverResp5: Project management with epics, sprints, and Kanban boards

docDocsConceptsArchitecture.serverResp7: Runner Agent service for automated sprint monitoring
docDocsConceptsArchitecture.serverResp8: RAG engine with pgvector (384d bge-small-en-v1.5) for context retrieval
docDocsConceptsArchitecture.serverResp10: Real-time event broadcasting via Laravel Reverb 1.10
docDocsConceptsArchitecture.requestLifecyclePara1: Every API request follows the standard Laravel pipeline: middleware (auth, rate limiting), controller, form request validation, service layer, Eloquent model, and API resource for response formatting.
docDocsConceptsArchitecture.agentPara1: The agent is a {nodejs} daemon that runs on the developer's machine. It manages local Claude Code processes via {nodePty}, streams terminal I/O over WebSocket, and handles discovery of local skills and MCP servers.

docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.title: Multi-Agent Coordination
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.lead: How multiple Claude Code instances collaborate on shared projects through ClaudeNest's task distribution, file locking, and vector-powered context sharing.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.overviewPara1: Complex software projects benefit from parallelism. Rather than a single Claude Code instance working through a long queue of tasks sequentially, ClaudeNest lets you run several instances simultaneously — each focused on an independent slice of work.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.overviewPara2: Concurrency introduces coordination problems: two agents must not edit the same file at the same time, and each agent needs to understand what the others have already done. ClaudeNest solves both problems with a centralized coordination layer built on three pillars:
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.pillarTaskDesc: Atomic task claiming ensures every unit of work is picked up by exactly one agent.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.pillarLockDesc: Pessimistic locking prevents simultaneous edits to the same file or directory.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.pillarCtxDesc: RAG-powered context chunks let every instance learn from what others have done.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.optionalTipDesc: Multi-agent coordination is a layer on top of ClaudeNest's core session management. A single agent with no shared project works perfectly for everyday use.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.sharedProjectsPara1: A shared project is the central record that links all coordination primitives together: instances, tasks, context chunks, and file locks all belong to a project. It also stores high-level metadata that every agent can read before starting work.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.metaSummary: One-paragraph plain-English description of the codebase
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.metaArchitecture: Key architectural decisions, patterns, and component relationships
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.metaConventions: Coding style, naming conventions, and mandatory patterns
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.metaCurrentFocus: The active sprint or goal (updated by team leads or orchestrators)
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.metaRecentChanges: Summary of the last significant changes made to the codebase
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.updatingContextPara: Keep the project metadata current so new instances start with accurate information. Agents should update current_focus and recent_changes after completing significant work.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.instancesPara1: Each running Claude Code process that connects to a shared project is registered as a Claude instance. Instances are identified by a string ID (typically machine-hostname-pid) and expose their status, current task, and token consumption via the API.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.instancesPara2: The server tracks last_activity_at for each instance. When an agent disconnects, the server automatically releases all file locks held by that instance and marks claimed tasks as pending again so other instances can pick them up.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.taskCoordinationPara1: Tasks are the primary unit of work in a multi-agent project. They describe a discrete, completable piece of work that a single agent can execute independently. The claiming mechanism is atomic — only one instance can ever hold a given task at the same time.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.creatingTasksPara: Tasks are created with a priority level and an optional list of dependencies on other task IDs. An agent (or an orchestrating script) typically creates all tasks upfront before any instances start claiming work.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.priorityCritical: Blocking tasks — must be resolved before any other work can proceed.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.priorityHigh: Important tasks that unblock multiple downstream items.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.priorityMedium: Standard implementation tasks with no special urgency.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.priorityLow: Nice-to-have improvements, docs, or minor refactors.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.atomicClaimingPara: When two agents call POST /api/tasks/{id}/claim simultaneously, the server uses a database-level atomic update (compare-and-swap on status) to guarantee only one succeeds. The losing agent receives a 409 Conflict and should request the next available task instead.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.taskStatusPara: Tasks transition from pending to in_progress on claim, then to review or done on completion. A task can be moved to blocked at any point if the agent discovers an unresolvable dependency, with a blocked_by reason attached for the human or orchestrator to resolve.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.taskDependenciesPara: The dependencies array contains task IDs that must reach done status before this task becomes claimable. The next-available endpoint automatically filters out tasks with unresolved dependencies, so agents never need to check this manually.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.completingTasksPara: If an agent cannot finish a task it has claimed (context window exhausted, blocked dependency discovered), it should release the task so another instance can attempt it:
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.fileLockingPara1: File locks use pessimistic locking: an agent acquires a lock before touching a file and holds it for the duration of its edits. Other agents that receive a file.locked event know to skip or defer any work on that path.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.lockExpiryPara: Locks expire after 30 minutes by default. If an agent anticipates longer work, it should extend the lock before it expires to avoid another agent claiming the same file.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.bulkLockingPara: For operations that span multiple files (e.g., a refactor touching several modules), request all locks in a single atomic call. The server either grants all requested locks or returns an error listing which paths are already held.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.releasingLocksPara: Always release locks explicitly when done. On agent disconnect, the server automatically releases all locks held by that instance's ID.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.forceReleasePara: If an agent crashes and its lock has not expired yet, a project owner can force-release a lock. Use with caution — only do this when you are certain the holding instance is no longer running.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.lockTipDesc: Prefer waiting for natural expiration (30 min) over force-releasing. If you need shorter expiry periods, set expires_at explicitly when creating the lock.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.contextSharingPara1: As each instance completes work, it contributes context chunks to the project's shared knowledge base. Chunks are embedded using bge-small-en-v1.5 (384-dimensional vectors) and stored in PostgreSQL with the pgvector extension. Any instance can then query the knowledge base using natural language and receive the most semantically relevant results.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.queryingContextPara: Before starting work on a task, an instance should query the shared context to avoid duplicating effort or making decisions that contradict prior work.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.chunkTaskCompletion: Summary of what was done when a task is marked complete
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.chunkDecision: Architectural or design decisions made during the session
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.chunkDiscovery: Findings about existing code structure or behaviour
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.chunkBlocker: Known problems or blockers that other agents should be aware of
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.chunkNote: General observations not tied to a specific task
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.importanceTipDesc: Set importance_score between 0.0 and 1.0. High-importance chunks (decisions, blockers) float to the top of search results when relevance scores are close. Default is 0.5.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.realtimePara1: All coordination events are broadcast over WebSocket to every agent and dashboard client subscribed to the projects.{id} private channel. This means agents learn about task claims, lock acquisitions, and peer completions within milliseconds — no polling required.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.eventTaskCreated: A new task was added to the board. Idle agents should call next-available to check if they can claim it.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.eventTaskClaimed: An instance claimed a task. Other agents can mark that task as unavailable in their local view.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.eventTaskCompleted: A task was completed. Any tasks that depended on it are now eligible for claiming.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.eventTaskReleased: An instance released a task back to the pool. Other instances should check next-available again.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.eventFileLocked: A file was locked by an instance. Agents should defer any work on that path until a corresponding file.unlocked event arrives.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.eventFileUnlocked: A lock was released. Waiting agents can now acquire the lock and proceed.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.interAgentMessagingPara: Agents can broadcast arbitrary messages to all other instances on the same project using the project.broadcast endpoint. This is useful for a leader agent to announce task decomposition results, or for any instance to signal an urgent blocker.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.patternsPara1: There is no single correct way to orchestrate agents. Choose the pattern that matches your project's dependency structure and the number of instances available.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.leaderWorkerPara: One dedicated leader instance decomposes the goal into tasks, creates them all upfront, then transitions to a worker role itself. Other instances connect and immediately start claiming from the shared task board.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.parallelTasksPara: The simplest pattern: all tasks are independent (no dependencies), all instances are equivalent. Each instance calls next-available in a loop, claims, works, completes, and repeats. The server automatically distributes load.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.sequentialPipelinePara: For workflows with strict ordering (e.g., design → implementation → tests → docs), create tasks with dependency chains. Instances running the later stages will block on next-available until upstream tasks complete.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.conflictResolutionPara1: Even with file locking and atomic task claiming, some conflict scenarios can arise. Here is how ClaudeNest handles each one.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.conflict1Title: Two agents claim the same task simultaneously
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.conflict1Desc: The server performs an atomic compare-and-swap: only the first request succeeds. The second agent receives 409 Conflict and must call next-available to find a different task. No manual intervention required.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.conflict2Title: Two agents request a lock on the same file
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.conflict2Desc: The first request succeeds and creates the lock record. The second request returns 423 Locked with the lock details (holder instance ID, expiry time). The blocked agent should wait for the file.unlocked WebSocket event before retrying.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.conflict3Title: An agent crashes while holding locks and a task
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.conflict3Desc: The server detects the WebSocket disconnect and automatically releases all file locks held by that instance ID and resets any claimed tasks back to pending. Other instances will pick them up on their next next-available poll.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.conflict4Title: Context chunks from two instances contradict each other
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.conflict4Desc: Context is append-only: contradicting chunks co-exist in the vector store. The most recent chunk for the same file path will generally surface higher in search results due to the importance_score and recency weighting. A human or orchestrator can delete stale chunks via DELETE /api/projects/{id}/context/chunks/{chunkId}.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.conflict5Title: A task's dependency is stuck in in_progress
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.conflict5Desc: If the holding instance has disconnected, the server resets the task to pending. If the instance is still running but slow, the orchestrator can move the dependency to blocked or done via PATCH /api/tasks/{id}, unblocking downstream work.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.observabilityTipDesc: The project activity log (GET /api/projects/{id}/activity) records every coordination event — claims, releases, lock acquisitions, context additions — with timestamps and instance IDs. Use it to debug unexpected states.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.autonomousPara: Beyond coordinating human-driven sessions, ClaudeNest can build a backlog on its own. Starting the orchestrator spawns a server-driven pool of Claude workers that claim the next available task, implement it, call task_complete, and immediately claim the next — a self-sustaining loop that needs no supervision. Workers run with bypassPermissions so they never stall on an approval dialog, and the planning agent can launch the pool itself with the execution_start tool right after drafting a plan.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.sandboxPara: Because workers run unattended with full permissions, each one is confined to a lightweight bubblewrap sandbox — an unprivileged, daemon-less Linux namespace sandbox (no Docker). The profile is "read-all, write-confined": the whole filesystem is visible read-only so the toolchain (node, git, compilers) works, but writes are restricted to the worker's own project directory, its session runtime, and a private /tmp. A worker therefore cannot modify system files, your home directory, or other projects. The agent installs bubblewrap automatically; set CLAUDENEST_SANDBOX=0 to opt out.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.freshContextPara: After completing a task, a worker is recycled: its session is terminated and replaced by a clean one before it claims the next task. Context never accumulates across the backlog, so each task starts from a focused, un-bloated state.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.resiliencePara: The loop is heartbeat-independent: a scheduled dispatcher nudges any worker that has gone silent, so a turn that ends on an API rate-limit is retried (with a cool-down and unlimited retries) instead of stalling. Tasks left in progress by a crashed worker are resumed first, and the agent reconnects to the server forever — a long outage or deploy never strands the pool.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.sprintPrPara: Completing a sprint asks the project's agent to open a pull request for the sprint's work: it creates a branch, commits the working tree, pushes, and runs gh pr create — then surfaces the PR URL on the project channel. The PR creation runs inside the same bubblewrap sandbox as the workers. Best-effort: if the remote or gh CLI is unavailable, the branch is still pushed.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.decompositionPara: Decomposing a PRD produces a plan structured into waves. When the plan is applied, each wave becomes a sprint (the first active, the rest in planning) and every task is attached to it — so real sprint progress drives the automatic pull request. Along the way, if the project has no context yet (summary, architecture, conventions), it is generated automatically from the PRD and indexed into the RAG store, never overwriting existing context.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.livingContextPara: Every completed task feeds the project's structured context: a rolling recent-changes log (bounded, newest first) and a current focus computed from real state (sprint progress, next task). Both are re-injected into every recycled worker's system prompt via context compilation — so the next worker reads the project's real state instead of a snapshot frozen at decomposition time.
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.gitTrackingHeading: Git tracking, pull requests and direct merge
docDocsConceptsMultiagentcoordination.gitTrackingPara: From the workspace, a Git tab shows the project's worktree state (branch, ahead/behind, changed files, last commit), the list of open pull requests, and lets you merge directly (squash, merge or rebase). Every git/gh command runs on the agent machine, inside the bubblewrap sandbox, and no GitHub token is stored server-side: the machine's own gh auth is reused.

docDocsConceptsRagembeddings.lead: How ClaudeNest uses pgvector and embeddings for context retrieval across multi-agent projects.
docDocsConceptsRagembeddings.whatIsRagPara1: (RAG) is a technique that enhances AI outputs by supplying relevant context at query time. Instead of relying solely on a model's training data, a RAG system retrieves semantically similar documents from a knowledge store and injects them into the prompt before generating a response.
docDocsConceptsRagembeddings.coreLoopIntro: The core loop has two phases:
docDocsConceptsRagembeddings.indexPhasePara1: Documents (code snippets, decisions, summaries) are converted into dense numerical vectors called

docDocsConceptsRagembeddings.queryPhasePara1: An incoming query is embedded into the same vector space. The nearest stored vectors are retrieved by
docDocsConceptsRagembeddings.queryPhasePara2: and returned as context chunks with relevance scores.
docDocsConceptsRagembeddings.whyRagPara1: When multiple Claude instances work on the same project simultaneously, they each have their own isolated context window. Without a shared knowledge store, Agent A has no awareness of the decisions or progress made by Agent B, leading to duplicated work, contradictory implementations, and wasted tokens.
docDocsConceptsRagembeddings.whyRagPara2b: scoped to each project. Every agent contributing a context chunk enriches the shared pool. Every agent querying the pool benefits from the collective knowledge — creating a form of persistent, searchable team memory.
docDocsConceptsRagembeddings.benefitSharedDesc: All agents start each task with access to the same architectural decisions and conventions.
docDocsConceptsRagembeddings.benefitDedupDesc: Before starting, an agent can query for prior completions on the same topic and avoid repeating it.
docDocsConceptsRagembeddings.benefitTokenDesc: Only the most relevant chunks are injected into each agent's context, preserving the context window.

docDocsConceptsRagembeddings.asyncEmbeddingPara1: Embedding generation is dispatched as a queued job so the HTTP response is returned immediately. The chunk appears in vector search results once the job completes (typically under 200 ms on local Ollama).
docDocsConceptsRagembeddings.queryPipelinePara1: Agents retrieve context by sending a natural language query. The server embeds the query text and runs a cosine similarity search, returning the top-k most semantically relevant chunks.

docDocsConceptsWebsocketprotocol.title: WebSocket Protocol
docDocsConceptsWebsocketprotocol.lead: Understanding ClaudeNest's real-time communication protocol built on Laravel Reverb.
docDocsConceptsWebsocketprotocol.overviewPara1: ClaudeNest relies on a persistent WebSocket layer for every piece of real-time interaction: terminal I/O streaming, machine health signals, multi-agent task coordination, and file-lock notifications. Without this channel the system degrades to a polling model, which is unsuitable for latency-sensitive terminal sessions and high-frequency agent events.
docDocsConceptsWebsocketprotocol.overviewPara2: The protocol is built on {reverb}, a first-party WebSocket server that integrates natively with Laravel's broadcasting system. Every state change in the backend — a session producing output, a task being claimed, a file being locked — is dispatched as a Laravel event that Reverb immediately delivers to all authenticated subscribers of the relevant channel.
docDocsConceptsWebsocketprotocol.featureDeliveryDesc: Terminal output chunks are pushed to clients as soon as the agent emits them, with no polling interval overhead.
docDocsConceptsWebsocketprotocol.featurePrivateDesc: All channels require a valid Sanctum token. Unauthorized subscription attempts are rejected before the channel is joined.
docDocsConceptsWebsocketprotocol.featureFanoutDesc: A single agent event is simultaneously delivered to the web dashboard, mobile app, and any other authenticated subscriber.
docDocsConceptsWebsocketprotocol.architecturePara1: The real-time stack is composed of two infrastructure pieces working in tandem: {reverb} as the WebSocket server and {redis} as the message broker between PHP worker processes and the Reverb server.
docDocsConceptsWebsocketprotocol.architecturePara2: When a Laravel controller dispatches a broadcast event, it is serialized and pushed onto a Redis channel. The queue worker picks it up, and Reverb reads from Redis to deliver the message to all connected WebSocket clients that have subscribed to the target channel. This decoupling means PHP workers never block on WebSocket delivery.
docDocsConceptsWebsocketprotocol.tipPusherDesc: Reverb implements the Pusher WebSocket protocol. Any Pusher-compatible client library — Laravel Echo, pusher-js, and most Socket.io adapters — works without modification. Raw {ws} connections use the agent's bespoke JSON envelope instead.
docDocsConceptsWebsocketprotocol.connectionPara1: Establishing a WebSocket connection follows a structured handshake. Clients must present a valid Sanctum bearer token in the HTTP upgrade request headers, after which they can subscribe to private channels that Reverb authorizes server-side.
docDocsConceptsWebsocketprotocol.step1Desc: The client opens a TCP connection and sends an HTTP {get} request with {upgrade}. The {auth} header is included in this initial request.
docDocsConceptsWebsocketprotocol.step2Desc: Reverb validates the token against Sanctum, then responds with {switching} to upgrade the connection. Invalid tokens receive a {forbidden} and the connection is closed.
docDocsConceptsWebsocketprotocol.step3Desc: The client sends a subscribe command for each private channel it needs. Reverb hits the Laravel channel authorization endpoint ({endpoint}) to verify that the authenticated user owns the subscribed resource.
docDocsConceptsWebsocketprotocol.step4Desc: Once subscribed, the client receives all broadcast events on that channel in real-time. The connection is kept alive by the heartbeat mechanism described below.
docDocsConceptsWebsocketprotocol.channelsPara1: All channels in ClaudeNest are {private}. Subscription is rejected unless the authenticated user owns or has access to the referenced resource. Channel authorization is defined in {channelsFile}.
docDocsConceptsWebsocketprotocol.eventsPara1: Events represent atomic state transitions in the system. Each event is broadcast on the channel of the resource it belongs to and received by all authenticated subscribers.
docDocsConceptsWebsocketprotocol.eventOutputDesc: Terminal output from the Claude Code PTY process. Delivered in chunks as data becomes available. Clients render this directly into xterm.js.
docDocsConceptsWebsocketprotocol.eventInputDesc: User keystrokes forwarded from the dashboard or mobile app to the agent managing the PTY. The agent writes this data directly to the pseudoterminal.
docDocsConceptsWebsocketprotocol.eventStatusDesc: Lifecycle state change for the session. Possible values: {values}.
docDocsConceptsWebsocketprotocol.eventResizeDesc: PTY dimension change. The agent calls {resize} upon receipt, which sends a {sigwinch} to the Claude Code process.
docDocsConceptsWebsocketprotocol.eventMachineStatusDesc: Machine connectivity state change. Possible values: {values}. Triggered by agent heartbeat or disconnect.
docDocsConceptsWebsocketprotocol.eventMachineCommandDesc: Server-initiated command sent to the agent. Used for session lifecycle operations, configuration updates, and capability refreshes.
docDocsConceptsWebsocketprotocol.eventTaskCreatedDesc: A new task was added to the shared project task board. All agents subscribed to the project channel see the new task immediately.
docDocsConceptsWebsocketprotocol.eventTaskClaimedDesc: An agent atomically claimed a pending task. Includes the instance ID so other agents know the task is no longer available.
docDocsConceptsWebsocketprotocol.eventTaskCompletedDesc: A task was completed successfully. Includes a summary of changes and the list of modified files for context synchronization.
docDocsConceptsWebsocketprotocol.eventTaskReleasedDesc: An agent released a previously claimed task back to the pending pool. Other agents can now claim it.
docDocsConceptsWebsocketprotocol.eventFileLockedDesc: A file was exclusively locked by an agent instance. Other agents should avoid editing this path until {unlocked} is received or the lock expires.
docDocsConceptsWebsocketprotocol.eventFileUnlockedDesc: A file lock was released, either explicitly by the agent or automatically when the {expires} timestamp passed.
docDocsConceptsWebsocketprotocol.eventProjectBroadcastDesc: A free-form message broadcast to all agents on the project. Used for coordination announcements, context updates, and custom agent-to-agent communication.
docDocsConceptsWebsocketprotocol.messageFormatPara1: All messages flowing through the WebSocket layer follow a consistent JSON structure. The exact envelope differs depending on the direction and the client type.
docDocsConceptsWebsocketprotocol.messageFormatServerDesc: Reverb wraps every Laravel event in the Pusher protocol format before delivery. Clients using Laravel Echo or pusher-js automatically unwrap this envelope.
docDocsConceptsWebsocketprotocol.messageFormatClientDesc: Client-originated events use whispers for ephemeral data — such as user input — that does not require server-side persistence. Whispers are relayed directly by Reverb without touching the Laravel application layer.
docDocsConceptsWebsocketprotocol.messageFormatAgentDesc: The Node.js agent uses a simpler envelope over its raw WebSocket connection. The server parses these messages and translates them into Laravel broadcast events for fan-out to other subscribers.
docDocsConceptsWebsocketprotocol.authPara1: WebSocket connections are secured with the same {sanctum} tokens used for the REST API. The token is passed in the HTTP upgrade request header, not as a query parameter, to avoid it appearing in server access logs.
docDocsConceptsWebsocketprotocol.authChannelAuthDesc: After the connection is established, each private channel subscription triggers a server-side authorization check. Reverb sends a {post} request to {endpoint} with the channel name and the user's socket ID. Laravel evaluates the channel callback defined in {channelsFile} and returns a signed auth token if the user is permitted.
docDocsConceptsWebsocketprotocol.authWarningTitle: Never pass tokens as query parameters
docDocsConceptsWebsocketprotocol.authWarningDesc: Query parameters appear in web server access logs and browser history. Always pass the Sanctum token in the {authHeader} header or via the Echo {echoOption} configuration option.
docDocsConceptsWebsocketprotocol.reconnectionPara1: Network interruptions are inevitable. All ClaudeNest clients implement an exponential backoff strategy with jitter to avoid thundering-herd reconnection storms after a server restart. The maximum reconnection delay is capped at {maxDelay} with a maximum of {maxAttempts} before the client emits a {event} event.
docDocsConceptsWebsocketprotocol.tipQueuingDesc: Agents buffer outbound messages in an in-memory queue while disconnected. On successful reconnection the queue is flushed in FIFO order. Messages older than 5 minutes are discarded to prevent delivering stale terminal output.
docDocsConceptsWebsocketprotocol.heartbeatPara1: Both the agent and the server exchange periodic keepalive frames to detect silent connection failures — scenarios where the TCP connection is broken but neither end receives a close frame (common with NAT timeouts or mobile network switches).
docDocsConceptsWebsocketprotocol.heartbeatReverbDesc: Laravel Reverb itself sends a Pusher-protocol {ping} frame to all connected clients every 30 seconds. Clients must respond with {pong} within 10 seconds or Reverb closes the connection, triggering the client's reconnection logic. Laravel Echo and pusher-js handle this automatically.
docDocsConceptsWebsocketprotocol.clientLibsPara1: ClaudeNest supports three distinct client integration patterns depending on the runtime environment.
docDocsConceptsWebsocketprotocol.libAgentNotes: Custom JSON envelope, message queue, backoff
docDocsConceptsWebsocketprotocol.libMobileNotes: Auto reconnect, background handling via AppState

docDocsCookbookMonitoring.title: Monitoring & Observability
docDocsCookbookMonitoring.lead: Monitor your ClaudeNest agents, sessions, and infrastructure performance in real time.
docDocsCookbookMonitoring.overviewPara: A healthy ClaudeNest deployment requires visibility at four levels: machine connectivity, session lifecycle, task throughput, and infrastructure health (PostgreSQL, Redis, Reverb). This guide covers the tools, endpoints, and patterns needed to keep everything observable.
docDocsCookbookMonitoring.metricMachinesDesc: Online status, heartbeats, agent version drift
docDocsCookbookMonitoring.metricSessionsDesc: Lifecycle state, token usage, cost tracking
docDocsCookbookMonitoring.metricTasksDesc: Claim rates, completion times, blocked tasks
docDocsCookbookMonitoring.metricInfraDesc: DB queries, Redis queues, WebSocket throughput
docDocsCookbookMonitoring.healthPara1: ClaudeNest exposes a GET /api/health endpoint that reports the status of all critical subsystems. Use it as the target for your load balancer or uptime monitor.
docDocsCookbookMonitoring.healthPara2: A non-200 response, or a status of "degraded" or "down" for any subsystem, should trigger an alert. The endpoint never requires authentication so it is safe to expose on a public path behind rate limiting.
docDocsCookbookMonitoring.machinePara1: Each agent pings the server every 30 seconds via the WebSocket heartbeat, updating the last_seen_at column on the machines table. A machine whose last_seen_at is older than 60 seconds should be considered offline.
docDocsCookbookMonitoring.machineWsPara: Subscribe to the private machines.{id} channel to receive status change events without polling.
docDocsCookbookMonitoring.machineCalloutBody: The agent_version field returned by GET /api/machines/{id} lets you detect outdated agents. Alert when the running version is more than one minor version behind the server's expected version.
docDocsCookbookMonitoring.sessionPara1: Sessions move through a defined lifecycle. Track each transition to detect stuck or runaway sessions.
docDocsCookbookMonitoring.sessionTokenPara: Each session accumulates total_tokens and total_cost. Query the session endpoint to retrieve current values without subscribing to WebSocket events.
docDocsCookbookMonitoring.sessionLogsPara: Full PTY output is stored in session_logs. Retrieve paginated logs for a session at any time, even after completion.
docDocsCookbookMonitoring.sessionCalloutBody: Set a max_tokens alert threshold. When total_tokens exceeds 80 % of your budget, send an in-app notification or terminate the session gracefully via DELETE /api/sessions/{id}.
docDocsCookbookMonitoring.taskPara1: The multi-agent task system exposes completion rates, average claim duration, and blocked task counts through the project stats endpoint.
docDocsCookbookMonitoring.taskBlockedPara: A task with status: "blocked" for more than a configurable threshold (e.g. 15 minutes) should trigger an alert. Poll the task list filtered by status:
docDocsCookbookMonitoring.wsPara1: Laravel Reverb exposes metrics on active connections and message throughput. Check the Reverb status endpoint or instrument your agent to emit connection events.
docDocsCookbookMonitoring.wsCalloutBody: High throughput from terminal output events (session.output) is expected during active sessions. Alert if the connection count drops to zero outside of a maintenance window — this indicates all agents have disconnected.
docDocsCookbookMonitoring.dbPara1: PostgreSQL performance directly impacts RAG query latency and task coordination. Monitor slow queries, index usage, and pgvector IVFFlat index health.
docDocsCookbookMonitoring.dbCalloutBody: When the context_chunks table grows beyond 1 million rows, rebuild the IVFFlat index with a higher lists value (e.g. 200) to maintain sub-10 ms vector search latency:
docDocsCookbookMonitoring.redisPara1: Redis backs the queue, cache, and session store. Monitor queue lengths and memory usage to catch bottlenecks before they impact agent throughput.
docDocsCookbookMonitoring.redisHorizonPara: If you use Laravel Horizon for queue supervision, it provides a built-in dashboard with queue depth, throughput, and failure rate metrics.
docDocsCookbookMonitoring.logPara1: ClaudeNest uses Laravel's structured logging. Configure the log channel to suit your stack — local file, Slack, or a log aggregator like Loki or Datadog.
docDocsCookbookMonitoring.logCalloutBody: The Node.js agent uses pino for structured JSON logs. Ship agent logs to the same aggregator as server logs and correlate them with the session_id field present in every agent log line.
docDocsCookbookMonitoring.alertPara1: Use Laravel's notification system to fire alerts when key thresholds are breached. The example below sends a webhook notification when a machine goes offline.
docDocsCookbookMonitoring.dashPara1: The ClaudeNest web dashboard provides real-time visibility into machines, sessions, and tasks. No additional setup is required — data is pushed via Reverb WebSocket events and displayed automatically.
docDocsCookbookMonitoring.dashItemMachines: Machines view — live online/offline status, last seen timestamp, active session count per machine.
docDocsCookbookMonitoring.dashItemSession: Session view — in-progress terminal output, token counter, elapsed time, and cost estimate updated every 5 seconds.
docDocsCookbookMonitoring.dashItemMultiAgent: Multi-agent view — task board with claim status, file lock map, and per-instance context token usage.
docDocsCookbookMonitoring.dashItemActivity: Activity log — chronological feed of all project events (context updates, task claims, file locks) queryable by instance or event type.

docDocsCookbookOauth.step1Body: Request the OAuth redirect URL from the API. The server generates a state parameter for CSRF protection.

docDocsCookbookOauth.securityNoteBody: Never expose tokens in client-side code or URLs. Store them in {httpOnly} cookies or secure storage (Keychain on iOS, Keystore on Android). Rotate tokens regularly.

docDocsCookbookSkillsdiscovery.title: Skills Discovery
docDocsCookbookSkillsdiscovery.lead: Learn how the ClaudeNest agent discovers skills on your machine, how to register them via the API, and how to manage categories, toggling, and bulk operations.
docDocsCookbookSkillsdiscovery.overviewPara1: Skills are modular capabilities that extend what Claude Code can do on a machine. They are discovered automatically by the agent or registered manually through the API. Each skill has a unique path identifier, a category, and can be enabled or disabled per machine.

docDocsCookbookSkillsdiscovery.agentDiscoveryPara1: When the agent starts, it automatically scans pre-configured directories and the system PATH for known tools and runtimes. Discovered capabilities are reported to the server as skills.

docDocsCookbookSkillsdiscovery.discoverPackageManagersText: -- npm, yarn, pnpm, pip, composer, cargo, gem.

docDocsCookbookSkillsdiscovery.registeringPara1: In addition to automatic discovery, you can register skills manually through the API. This is useful for custom scripts or tools that the agent cannot auto-detect.
docDocsCookbookSkillsdiscovery.categoriesPara1: Skills are organized into categories for easier management. The agent assigns categories automatically during discovery, but you can override them when registering manually.
docDocsCookbookSkillsdiscovery.togglingPara1: Each skill can be individually enabled or disabled. Disabled skills are not made available to Claude Code sessions. This is useful for restricting access to certain tools in production environments.
docDocsCookbookSkillsdiscovery.bulkOperationsPara1: Update multiple skills at once using the bulk endpoint. This supports enabling, disabling, or updating metadata for many skills in a single request.

docDocsGuidesAgentsetup.title: Agent Setup
docDocsGuidesAgentsetup.lead: Install and configure the ClaudeNest agent on your machine. The agent is a lightweight daemon that connects to the server, manages PTY sessions, and relays terminal I/O in real time.
docDocsGuidesAgentsetup.installationIntro: The agent is distributed as an npm package. You can install it globally or run it from a cloned repository.
docDocsGuidesAgentsetup.nodeRequirement: The agent requires Node.js 24 LTS or later. On Linux and macOS the node-pty native add-on is compiled during install, so you also need a C++ toolchain (build-essential / Xcode CLI tools).

docDocsGuidesFilelocking.title: File Locking
docDocsGuidesFilelocking.lead: Prevent conflicts when multiple agents edit the same files. File-level locks give an agent an exclusive claim on a path for a configurable duration; hooks enforce it at edit time.
docDocsGuidesFilelocking.whyPara1: When several Claude instances work on the same project simultaneously, two agents might try to modify the same file at the same time. Without coordination the result is merge conflicts, overwritten work, or inconsistent state.
docDocsGuidesFilelocking.whyPara2: ClaudeNest's file locking system solves this by letting an instance acquire an exclusive lock on a file path before editing it. Other instances can check whether a file is locked and either wait or choose a different file to work on.
docDocsGuidesFilelocking.keyCharacteristics: Key characteristics of the locking system:
docDocsGuidesFilelocking.keyItem2: Each lock has an expiration time (default 30 minutes) to prevent deadlocks
docDocsGuidesFilelocking.keyItem3: Locks can be extended if the work takes longer than expected
docDocsGuidesFilelocking.keyItem5: Disconnected instances have their locks released automatically
docDocsGuidesFilelocking.acquirePara1: Before editing a file, an instance requests a lock. The server grants the lock only if the file is not already locked by another instance.
docDocsGuidesFilelocking.acquireConflictIntro: If the file is already locked, the server returns a
docDocsGuidesFilelocking.acquireConflictIntroSuffix: response with details about the current lock holder:
docDocsGuidesFilelocking.acquireTip: Always check for a 409 response and implement a retry or fallback strategy in your agent logic.
docDocsGuidesFilelocking.checkPara1: Before attempting to lock a file, you can check whether it is already locked. This is useful for planning which files to work on next.
docDocsGuidesFilelocking.extendPara1: If the work is taking longer than the original expiration window, the lock holder can extend the lock duration. Only the instance that owns the lock can extend it.
docDocsGuidesFilelocking.atomicPara1b: to ensure true atomicity. Even when two instances send a lock request at exactly the same millisecond, only one succeeds. The losing request immediately receives a
docDocsGuidesFilelocking.atomicPara1c: without any risk of both believing they hold the lock.
docDocsGuidesFilelocking.atomicPara2: This guarantee is stronger than application-level checks. You do not need to implement your own mutex or retry loop beyond the standard 409 handling.
docDocsGuidesFilelocking.taskLockPara1a: When an instance claims a task via
docDocsGuidesFilelocking.taskLockPara1b: , any file paths listed in the task's
docDocsGuidesFilelocking.taskLockPara1c: array are automatically locked for that instance. This means you rarely need to call the lock endpoints directly for normal task work.
docDocsGuidesFilelocking.taskLockPara2a: Conversely, when a task is completed (
docDocsGuidesFilelocking.taskLockPara2c: ), all locks held by the instance for those files are automatically released. This keeps lock cleanup inside the task lifecycle rather than requiring explicit teardown code.
docDocsGuidesFilelocking.taskLockTipA: The auto-lock behaviour applies only to files declared in the task's
docDocsGuidesFilelocking.taskLockTipB: field at claim time. Files opened ad hoc during the task must still be locked manually via
docDocsGuidesFilelocking.heartbeatPara1: The agent daemon sends a heartbeat to the server every 60 seconds for each active session. If a session holds locks whose expiration is within 5 minutes of the current time, the server automatically extends those locks by 15 minutes. This prevents locks from expiring mid-task without requiring the agent to poll the extend endpoint.
docDocsGuidesFilelocking.heartbeatPara2b: manually at any time if you need a longer window or want to extend locks held outside an active session.
docDocsGuidesFilelocking.conflictsPara1: Before starting a large task that touches many files, check all of them in a single request using the conflicts endpoint. The server returns only the files that are currently locked, so you can decide whether to wait, reassign the task, or proceed with the unlocked subset.
docDocsGuidesFilelocking.bulkPara1: When a task involves multiple files, you can lock them all in a single atomic request. Either all locks succeed or none are acquired, which prevents partial-lock scenarios.
docDocsGuidesFilelocking.bulkTip: Bulk locking is atomic: if any file is already locked by another instance, the entire request fails and no locks are created.
docDocsGuidesFilelocking.releasePara1: When the instance finishes editing, it should release the lock so other agents can work on the file. You can release a single lock or all locks held by an instance at once.
docDocsGuidesFilelocking.forceReleasePara1: Project owners can force-release any lock, regardless of who holds it. This is useful when an instance has disconnected without cleaning up.

docDocsGuidesGettingstarted.title: Getting Started
docDocsGuidesGettingstarted.lead: ClaudeNest is a remote Claude Code orchestration platform that lets you control, coordinate, and monitor multiple Claude Code instances from anywhere.
docDocsGuidesGettingstarted.overviewPara1: ClaudeNest transforms Claude Code from a local-only tool into a fully remote, multi-agent system. Whether you need to run Claude on a powerful server, coordinate multiple instances on the same codebase, or monitor sessions from your phone, ClaudeNest provides the infrastructure to make it happen.
docDocsGuidesGettingstarted.capRemoteAccessText: Control Claude Code instances running on any machine from a web dashboard or mobile app
docDocsGuidesGettingstarted.capMultiAgentText: Run multiple Claude instances on the same project with shared context, task coordination, and file locking
docDocsGuidesGettingstarted.capContextRagText: pgvector-powered retrieval augmented generation so every agent shares project understanding
docDocsGuidesGettingstarted.capRealTimeText: WebSocket-based bidirectional streaming for terminal I/O
docDocsGuidesGettingstarted.capMcpText: Discover and manage Model Context Protocol servers across your machines
docDocsGuidesGettingstarted.architecturePara1: ClaudeNest follows a hub-and-spoke architecture with three main components that communicate in real time:
docDocsGuidesGettingstarted.serverHubPara: The central Laravel 13 application handles authentication, API routing, WebSocket relay via Laravel Reverb, and persistent storage in PostgreSQL with pgvector for embeddings. It also serves the Vue.js web dashboard.
docDocsGuidesGettingstarted.agentSpokePara1: A lightweight Node.js daemon that runs on each machine you want to control. It manages local Claude Code processes via
docDocsGuidesGettingstarted.agentSpokePara2: , streams terminal output over WebSocket, and handles session lifecycle.
docDocsGuidesGettingstarted.clientsPara: Users interact with ClaudeNest through the web dashboard (Vue.js + xterm.js), native mobile apps (React Native), or directly via the REST API. All clients connect to the server, which relays commands to the appropriate agent.
docDocsGuidesGettingstarted.architectureTip: The agent connects outbound to the server via WebSocket, so no inbound ports need to be opened on the machine running Claude Code.
docDocsGuidesGettingstarted.prerequisitesIntro: Before setting up ClaudeNest, make sure you have the following:
docDocsGuidesGettingstarted.reqServerPhp: PHP 8.4+ with required extensions (pgsql, redis, pcntl)
docDocsGuidesGettingstarted.reqServerRedis: Redis 7+ for caching, queues, and broadcasting
docDocsGuidesGettingstarted.reqServerNode: Node.js 24+ and npm (for building the frontend)
docDocsGuidesGettingstarted.reqAgentCli: Claude Code CLI installed and authenticated
docDocsGuidesGettingstarted.reqAgentNetwork: Network access to the ClaudeNest server (outbound WebSocket)
docDocsGuidesGettingstarted.reqDevEditor: A code editor with Vue.js and PHP support
docDocsGuidesGettingstarted.prerequisitesTipPre: If you prefer Docker, you can skip the individual prerequisites and use
docDocsGuidesGettingstarted.prerequisitesTipPost: to start all services at once.
